四级汇总词汇 · 08英文原文

The Boy Who Asked to Read Aloud

主动开口朗读的男孩 · 648 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1At an elementary school, a gifted math pupil named Tao seldom read aloud. He could manage a hard fraction in his head and draw the answer on the blackboard. A short sentence made him anxious. His tutor first met him on the playground beside the kindergarten. A toddler had fallen, and Tao had stopped to comfort her. He had shown more patience with the child than he ever showed with himself. His tutor asked him to use that same patience when he came for a reading tutorial.

2Tao's stepfather wanted him to try an arithmetic olympiad. He was proud of the boy's grade and thought remedial work might embarrass him. His dad had once won the same contest as a teen. Tao was conscious of that pride. At home he could spell a word to his stepsister. On campus he pretended to be bored. A notice about fifty questions had frightened him less than the thought of one mistake in front of friends. The tutor proposed a quiet session to see where his aptitude actually lay.

3They began with a picture from the preschool nursery. An adventurous toddler had drawn a lioness, an orphan kitten, and a fat mouse beside a door. She wanted to know which animal could come inside. Tao understood the drawing but struggled to read its message. A deaf learner and a partially blind girl joined him. A female assistant described the pictures aloud. Each pupil could sign or draw an answer. One drew a magnet on the door. Tao chose three words and gave a straightforward reply. It was a more useful way to socialize than rushing past words he could not read.

4The headmistress had planned an optional afternoon elective for proficient readers. Its enrollment form asked pupils to write why they wanted admission. Tao saw it and assumed the class was selective. The tutor showed him a separate intake for pupils who needed to build comprehension. She asked him to imagine writing a question for a younger child. He made up a story about a brave youngster who found a lost kitten. He was fascinated to see his stepsister finish it without help.

5At home his stepsister said, "I wanna hear it again." Their babysitter, a student from a nearby dorm, said she could listen after the toddler's nap. Tao stayed awake while his sister began to snore. The girl woke happily, pulled off a wool beanie, and asked him to read. He missed a word, shed a tear, and started to weep. She gave him a hug and asked what the kitten did next. That question turned a tiring exercise into a story again.

6At daycare, children asked why the male teacher seldom read stories about mothers. Tao helped them visualize a family. One drew an adorable lioness with cubs. Another drew an orphanage. A parent praised the conversation about parenting. "That's my daddy," one child said. Another drew her mommy.

7The contest took place on the same afternoon as the optional class. His stepfather thought the contest was almost obligatory. Now Tao confessed he had entered mainly to please his family. He asked to attend the reading group first. He could still strive in math, and adulthood was far away. The tutor said the choice need not depend on persuasion or obedience. Each week he would solve one problem for a younger pupil and read a short story of his choice.

8Several months later Tao helped a freshman find the class list on a different campus. The new pupil was lonely and too scared to ask the way. Tao read the list aloud and walked with him to the room. Inside, the younger group had drawn a circle around the picture of a kitten. The headmistress asked who wanted to start the next story. Tao straightened his sheet of paper. Before anyone could persuade him, he volunteered to read.

四级汇总词汇 · 08中文译文

主动开口朗读的男孩

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1小学里有个擅长数学的学生小陶，平时很少出声朗读。他能心算很难的分数题，再把答案画在黑板上，一句短句却能让他焦虑。家教老师第一次见他是在幼儿园旁的操场上。一个孩子摔倒，他停下来安慰她。他对孩子比对自己耐心得多。老师请他来上阅读辅导时，也给自己同样的耐心。

2小陶的继父想让他参加算术竞赛。他为孩子的成绩骄傲，觉得补习会让小陶难堪。继父年轻时还赢过同样的比赛。小陶很清楚家人有多看重这一点。他在家能给继妹拼出一个单词，在学校却总装作无聊。公告上的五十道题还不如当朋友面读错一个词吓人。老师提议先安静地试一回，看看他的能力究竟表现在哪里。

3他们先看幼儿班的一张画。一个爱冒险的小孩子在门边画了母狮、无家可归的小猫和一只胖老鼠，想知道谁能进门。小陶看得懂画，却读不出文字。一名失聪学生和一个视力部分受损的女孩加入了他们。女助教把画面讲出来，学生可以用手语或画图回答。有人给门画上一块磁铁。小陶挑了三个词，给出一个直接的回答。这比匆匆跳过读不出的字更能和别人交流。

4校长原打算为读得熟练的学生开一门自选午间课。报名表问想入班的理由，小陶以为它只收水平高的人。老师给他看另一组招生，那组是给需要提高理解能力的学生。她让他想象自己给更小的孩子写一个问题。他编了个勇敢的小孩找到迷路小猫的故事，看见继妹不用帮助就读完时，觉得十分有意思。

5在家里，继妹说她还想再听一遍。住在附近宿舍的临时保姆说，等小孩子睡醒再听。妹妹打呼噜时，小陶还醒着。女孩高兴地醒过来，摘掉毛线帽，要他朗读。他读漏一个词，掉下眼泪。妹妹抱了他一下，问小猫后来做了什么。这个问题把累人的练习变回了一个故事。

6在托儿所，孩子们问男老师为什么很少读关于妈妈的故事。小陶帮他们想象一个家庭。有人画了一只可爱的母狮和幼崽，有人画了孤儿院。一位家长很高兴大家聊起怎样养育孩子。一个孩子说那是我爸爸，另一个则画了自己的妈妈。

7竞赛和选修课在同一个下午。继父觉得竞赛几乎是必选项。小陶承认，报名主要是为了让家人高兴。他想先去阅读小组。他仍然可以努力学数学，离成年还早。老师说，选择不必靠劝说或听话来决定。每周他给一个小学生解一道题，再读一篇自己挑的故事。

8几个月后，小陶在另一个校区帮新生找名单。新生孤零零的，不敢问路。小陶把名单读给他听，带他走进教室。里面的小朋友已经在小猫的图外画了一个圈。校长问谁想先读接下来的故事。小陶把纸理平，还没人来劝他，他已经主动举手。
